question: Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions causing secondary amenorrhoea and infertility) is a recognised complication of over-vigorous endometrial curettage, particularly when performed in the postpartum uterus.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — this statement is true. Asherman syndrome is caused by over-curettage destroying the endometrial basalis, leading to intrauterine adhesions. The postpartum uterus is at highest risk. It is a preventable complication that can cause secondary infertility.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Asherman syndrome results from destruction of the basalis layer of the endometrium during aggressive curettage. Risk is highest when curettage is performed on a postpartum or post-abortal uterus because the endometrium is thinner and more vulnerable.
